title: The Alpine Chalet Fink Roof
subtitle: Span a 12m roof ridge and withstand heavy snowpack without collapse.
scenario: A ski resort lodge in the Swiss Alps requires a timber-and-steel pitched roof truss. Heavy winter snow accumulations apply a uniform distributed vertical snowpack load across the upper rafters (-15 kN per node).
backgroundBriefing: The Fink truss is a classic pitched roof design characterized by V-shaped web sub-triangulation that keeps compression web members short and perpendicular to the sloping top chords. Pinned at one wall and resting on a roller at the opposite wall to accommodate thermal expansion.
pedagogicalTakeaways: Pitched rafters carry both axial compression and outward thrust against the walls.
The bottom tie member is in pure tension, holding the two roof walls together.
Fink web geometry keeps diagonal struts short, minimizing Euler buckling risk.
